questions.question_text: For which of the following classes of substances does DSM-IV-TR recognize only the diagnoses dependence and withdrawal?
A positive predictor of response to electroconvulsive therapy (ECT) in patients with unipolar depression is:

options.text: Failure to respond to one or more antidepressants prior to receiving ECT

questions.question_text: A number of empirically based psychosocial interventions are available for treating substance use disorders. Which of the following interventions uses a combination of cognitive-behavioral therapy groups, family education groups, social support groups, individual counseling, regular drug testing, and optional 12-Step group attendance?

Which of the following medications used for the treatment of alcohol dependence has as its mechanism of action the restoration of balance between excitatory glutamate and inhibitory γ-aminobutyric acid (GABA) neurotransmitter systems?
Which of the following statements concerning women and substance use disorders is true?

options.text: Women make up approximately 50% of patients in traditional treatment centers for alcohol dependence in the United States
Women are more likely to binge drink, drink with others, and drink the same quantities of alcohol as men
Women with alcohol use disorders are more likely to present for treatment of other problems, such as marital difficulties, physical illness, or emotional problems
Women are less likely than men to have been introduced to heroin or methamphetamine by a significant other
In 2003-2004, almost 20% of pregnant women were past-month users of illicit drugs

correct_answer.text: Women with alcohol use disorders are more likely to present for treatment of other problems, such as marital difficulties, physical illness, or emotional problems

correct_answers.text: Women with alcohol use disorders are more likely to present for treatment of other problems, such as marital difficulties, physical illness, or emotional problems

questions.question_text: An important theoretical issue is whether the personality disorders are best classified as dimensions or categories. Which of the following arguments supports a categorical approach to personality disorder classification?

options.text: The thresholds for diagnosing personality disorders are arbitrary
Excessive diagnostic co-occurrence between personality disorders has been observed in many studies
The residual category of personality disorder not otherwise specified (NOS) may be the most commonly assigned personality disorder diagnosis in clinical practice
There is considerable heterogeneity of features among patients receiving the same diagnosis
Categorical models better reflect how clinicians think about pathological syndromes

correct_answer.text: The thresholds for diagnosing personality disorders are arbitrary

correct_answers.text: The thresholds for diagnosing personality disorders are arbitrary

questions.question_text: You are called to the emergency room to evaluate a male patient brought in by the police for bizarre behavior (i.e., talking to himself in public, gesturing for no apparent reason). The patient is unkempt; his speech is odd and idiosyncratic, although there is no overt psychosis. A drug screen is negative. There is no information on whether gradual social deterioration has occurred. Your preliminary diagnosis is a personality disorder. Which of the following is most likely?

Pharmacological treatment strategies for borderline personality disorder have targeted affective dysregulation, impulsivity, and psychotic-like features. Which of the following medications commonly prescribed for the management of impulsivity may potentially worsen symptoms?

The characterization of specific cytochrome P450 (CYP) enzymes has made it possible to understand and predict many drug-drug interactions. Which of the following CYP enzymes is essential for the metabolism of tricyclic antidepressants (TCAs)?
Tricyclic antidepressants (TCAs) are known for their effects on multiple transmitter systems. Which of the following is not a pharmacological property of TCAs?

Bupropion is an alternative antidepressant that may be particularly useful in patients with selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor (SSRI)-induced sexual side effects. Which of the following side effects is not associated with bupropion?

Mirtazapine is an antidepressant with a series of receptor-specific activities that explain its effects on mood disorder symptoms and its particular side-effect profile. Which of the following is not a mechanism associated with mirtazapine?

options.text: Antagonism of α2 noradrenergic autoreceptors and heteroreceptors

questions.question_text: Maintenance treatment is often needed because of the recurring nature of the illness. Some patient groups may be at particular risk for recurrence and thus should be more strongly considered for maintenance therapy. According to Keller (2001), all of the following groups of depressed patients should be considered for maintenance therapy except?

options.text: Patients with three or more episodes of major depression
Patients with two or more episodes of major depression and a family history of a mood disorder
Patients with rapid recurrence of depressive episodes
Patients with a younger age at onset of depression
Patients with severe episodes of depression

correct_answer.text: Patients with a younger age at onset of depression

correct_answers.text: Patients with a younger age at onset of depression

questions.question_text: The Clinical Antipsychotic Trials of Intervention Effectiveness (CATIE) study examined numerous antipsychotic agents for their clinical utility and side effect burden. Which of the following antipsychotic medications examined in the CATIE study was associated with improvements in metabolic parameters?

Lithium is a very effective treatment for mania but is associated with a number of troubling side effects, including nephrogenic diabetes insipidus (NDI). Prevention and management strategies for NDI include all of the following except?

Valproate is commonly used in the treatment of bipolar disorders. Valproate is associated with numerous side effects which may limit its use. Which of the following side effects is not associated with valproate?

Several key principles apply to the exercise of moral behavior and are especially applicable to medical ethics. The movement toward "parity" legislation to ensure that provision of care for mental illness is analogous to care for systemic illness illustrates the ethical principle of:

In the "four-topics method" of ethical decision making (Jansen et al. 1998), data gathering about a particular dilemma is first accomplished and ethical reasoning is then applied. The case of a terminal cancer patient who refuses chemotherapy represents a conflict between which two of this model's four topics?

options.text: Patient quality of life versus contextual or external influences
Clinical indications versus contextual or external influences
Patient quality of life versus patient preferences
Patient quality of life versus clinical indications

correct_answer.text: Clinical indications versus contextual or external influences

correct_answers.text: Clinical indications versus contextual or external influences

questions.question_text: Patients with atients have been called "errant" therapists; this represents a significant ethical violation. Gabbard (1999; Gabbard and Lester 1995) has classified such therapists according to four psychodynamic groups. Which of the following is not included in Gabbard's classification scheme?

options.text: Therapists who give in to patient requests for sex as "masochistic surrender"
"Lovesick" therapists who become infatuated with a particular patient
"Predatory" therapists (often with paraphilias) who prey on vulnerable patients
Psychotic therapists who are acting on a delusion
Therapists who are disinhibited because of active abuse of substances

correct_answer.text: Therapists who are disinhibited because of active abuse of substances

correct_answers.text: Therapists who are disinhibited because of active abuse of substances

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements regarding psychiatric patients' participation in clinical research is false?

options.text: Because they are a "vulnerable population," psychiatric patients should be globally prohibited from research participation
Medication use in "washout" periods should be specified
The use of placebo controls should be disclosed
Institutional Review Board review and privacy safeguards need to be clear
Informed consent must be strictly observed

correct_answer.text: Because they are a "vulnerable population," psychiatric patients should be globally prohibited from research participation

correct_answers.text: Because they are a "vulnerable population," psychiatric patients should be globally prohibited from research participation

questions.question_text: A patient requests that her psychiatrist document a "less stigmatizing" illness in her chart instead of her actual diagnosis. This psychiatrist's ethical dilemma is between which two ethical principles?
Many changes in sleep architecture are seen in aging, and these changes may play a role in late-life insomnia. Which of the following is a typical sleep architecture change affecting the elderly?

options.text: Decreased percentages of Stage 1 and 2 sleep
Increased percentages of Stage 3 and 4 sleep
Decreased absolute amounts of REM sleep

correct_answer.text: Decreased absolute amounts of REM sleep

correct_answers.text: Decreased absolute amounts of REM sleep

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements regarding hypochondriasis in the elderly is true?

options.text: The distinction between somatic delusions and hypochondriasis is a difficult one to make clinically in older patients
Hypochondriacal complaints in the elderly are usually about the cardiovascular system
Interpreting hypochondriasis as a manifestation of past guilt being directed to physical symptoms usually clears hypochondriasis rapidly
Depression is accompanied by excess physical concerns only in the elderly
Suicide risk is increased in depressed elders with comorbid hypochondriacal concerns

correct_answer.text: Suicide risk is increased in depressed elders with comorbid hypochondriacal concerns

correct_answers.text: Suicide risk is increased in depressed elders with comorbid hypochondriacal concerns

questions.question_text: Postpartum depression is a commonly encountered clinical problem among women of childbearing age. Which of the following regarding this condition is true?

options.text: The postpartum-onset specifier in DSM-IV-TR for depression requires onset within 12 weeks of delivery
A history of major depression increases the risk of postpartum depression to 50%
Postpartum depression shows a more robust response to tricyclic antidepressants (TCAs) than to selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors (SSRIs)

For postpartum patients with a history of postpartum depression, prophylaxis with antidepressants beginning within 48 hours postpartum has consistently shown a protective effect against developing postpartum depression
Despite the likely hormonal genesis of much postpartum depression, estrogen is not considered a primary treatment

correct_answer.text: A history of major depression increases the risk of postpartum depression to 50%

correct_answers.text: A history of major depression increases the risk of postpartum depression to 50%

questions.question_text: Women at menopause may present with depression. In the diagnosis and management of this condition, several risk factors may be considered. Which of the following psychiatric, systemic, or social factor is not associated with increased risk of perimenopausal depression?

options.text: Parental death and children leaving home ("empty nest")

questions.question_text: There are a number of other impulse-control disorders that are not included in DSM-IVTR as a distinct category but are categorized as impulse-control disorders not otherwise specified (NOS) in DSM-IV-TR. Which of the following is one of those NOS categories?
Which of the following statements concerning kleptomania is true?

options.text: Patients with kleptomania often report amnesia surrounding the act of shoplifting
The majority of patients with kleptomania are men
The severity of kleptomania symptoms varies by gender, with males having more severe symptoms
The most common personality disorder reported in patients with kleptomania is antisocial personality disorder
Kleptomania has been found to be quite rare in psychiatric inpatients

correct_answer.text: Kleptomania has been found to be quite rare in psychiatric inpatients

correct_answers.text: Kleptomania has been found to be quite rare in psychiatric inpatients

questions.question_text: Which of the following disorders has been found to frequently co-occur with pathological gambling?
Which type of parasomnia occurs during periods of non-rapid eye movement (NREM) stage 2-4 sleep at any time during the night and is associated with low autonomic activity?
Rett's disorder:

options.text: Is typically diagnosed before the first year of life
Is found almost exclusively in males
May be diagnosed when there is evidence of intrauterine growth retardation
Is characterized by a period of decelerated head growth
Is associated with decreased daytime and increased nighttime sleep

correct_answer.text: Is characterized by a period of decelerated head growth

correct_answers.text: Is characterized by a period of decelerated head growth

questions.question_text: Children with Asperger's disorder:

options.text: Have clinically significant delay in language
May represent a lower-functioning portion of an autistic disorder spectrum
Have restricted and repetitive interests and behaviors

correct_answer.text: Have restricted and repetitive interests and behaviors

correct_answers.text: Have restricted and repetitive interests and behaviors

questions.question_text: Tourette's disorder is differentiated from other tic disorders by which of the following?

options.text: Presence of prodromal sensations to perform the tic

questions.question_text: The adjustment disorder diagnosis in DSM-IV-TR has been found to have certain advantages and disadvantages for patients and clinicians. Which of the following is the major disadvantage of using the diagnosis?

options.text: The concept of temporary emotional symptoms resulting from a stressful life event seems more of a normal human reaction than a pathological diagnostic state
The diagnosis's more benign course allows clinicians to be more prognostically optimistic
Medical insurance carriers do not consider the diagnosis to be a preexisting condition when evaluating a patient's risk
The concept of the stressor lacks quantifiable and qualifiable guidelines, contributing to the vague and nonspecific nature of the diagnosis

correct_answer.text: The concept of the stressor lacks quantifiable and qualifiable guidelines, contributing to the vague and nonspecific nature of the diagnosis

correct_answers.text: The concept of the stressor lacks quantifiable and qualifiable guidelines, contributing to the vague and nonspecific nature of the diagnosis

questions.question_text: Which of the following features is descriptive of depersonalization disorder?

options.text: Patients frequently have impaired reality testing
Patients are rarely distressed by the symptoms

questions.question_text: The general trend toward the development of brief psychotherapy models involved several points of conceptual differentiation from the original model of psychoanalysis. Which of the following is not characteristic of the role or stance of the therapist in brief models compared with therapist behavior in psychoanalysis?

options.text: The therapist assumes a more active role in promoting patient health
Change in brief psychotherapy is primarily due to the acquisition of insight, not of contemporary experience
The therapist's main role is to promote self-exploration by the patient
The therapist should avoid the "prescription" of out-of-session homework
The therapist should resist the role of problem solver

correct_answer.text: Change in brief psychotherapy is primarily due to the acquisition of insight, not of contemporary experience

correct_answers.text: Change in brief psychotherapy is primarily due to the acquisition of insight, not of contemporary experience

questions.question_text: Psychodynamic brief therapies retain the theoretical and conceptual heritage of psychoanalysis with some important operational modifications. Which of the following is not a specific feature of short-term psychodynamic psychotherapy?

options.text: Active provision of positive relational experiences in therapy
A primary focus on therapist interpretation of material presented by the patient
Creation of heightened emotional contexts for change

correct_answer.text: Active provision of positive relational experiences in therapy

correct_answers.text: Active provision of positive relational experiences in therapy

questions.question_text: Interpersonal psychotherapy (IPT) is another brief therapy model with a specific theoretical basis and technical approach. Which of the following is not considered an appropriate therapy focus in the IPT approach?

options.text: Deep exploration of past, not current, relational problems
Phase of life role transitions, such as career changes
Interpersonal sensitivity (e.g., a difficulty with rejection)

correct_answer.text: Deep exploration of past, not current, relational problems

correct_answers.text: Deep exploration of past, not current, relational problems

questions.question_text: Supportive psychotherapy depends on clearly defined techniques designed to achieve specific goals. Which of the following concerning supportive interventions is true?

options.text: Anxiety is deliberately provoked to motivate change in maladaptive behavior
The therapist focuses more on past experiences than on the here and now
The therapeutic relationship is addressed through an intense focus on the transference
Resistance is directly confronted as maladaptive
Adaptive defenses are strengthened and supported

correct_answer.text: The therapist focuses more on past experiences than on the here and now

correct_answers.text: The therapist focuses more on past experiences than on the here and now

questions.question_text: Comparisons of depressed and anxious patients have revealed differences between the two groups as well as common features of the disorders. Which of the following cognitive responses to environmental stimuli has been found to be more characteristic of anxious patients than of depressed patients?

options.text: Underestimation of the amount of positive feedback
Attentional bias toward potentially threatening stimuli

correct_answer.text: Attentional bias toward potentially threatening stimuli

correct_answers.text: Attentional bias toward potentially threatening stimuli

questions.question_text: Cognitive therapy begins with an assessment and initial case formulation before therapy proceeds. Which of the following is not an element of case conceptualization?

options.text: Outline of major parts of the history and mental status examination
Detail of three or more examples from the patient's life where the cognitive model applies
Listing of patient weaknesses and vulnerabilities
A working hypothesis and treatment plan

correct_answer.text: Listing of patient weaknesses and vulnerabilities

correct_answers.text: Listing of patient weaknesses and vulnerabilities

questions.question_text: The process of modifying automatic thoughts involves several separate psychotherapeutic processes. When the therapist helps the patient to examine automatic thoughts to reconceptualize feared outcomes in a manner that facilitates problem solving, he or she is using which of the following techniques?

Initially developed as a treatment for major depressive disorders, interpersonal psychotherapy (IPT) has been modified and applied to other psychiatric disorders. IPT is not currently considered an effective psychotherapy model for which of the following disorders?
Which of the following is not one of the four interpersonal problem areas emphasized in the interpersonal psychotherapy (IPT) model?

The National Institute of Mental Health Treatment of Depression Collaborative Research Program outpatients were randomly assigned to interpersonal psychotherapy (IPT), cognitive-behavioral therapy (CBT), or medication (either imipramine or placebo) plus clinical management. Which of the following statements concerning outcomes from this study is true?

options.text: Patients with mild depression improved with IPT but not CBT
Imipramine did not work faster than IPT
IPT was comparable to imipramine on several outcome measures
CBT was superior to placebo for severe depression
IPT was not superior to placebo for severe depression

correct_answer.text: IPT was comparable to imipramine on several outcome measures

correct_answers.text: IPT was comparable to imipramine on several outcome measures

questions.question_text: You evaluate a 35-year-old male patient in an outpatient clinic who has experienced psychotic symptoms confined to one nonbizarre delusion for the past 3-5 years. He has exhibited minimal decline in social and occupational functioning and minimal change in symptoms over time. His symptoms have been refractory to previous treatments. On the basis of this limited clinical information, the most likely diagnosis is:

Four recent epidemiological studies published over a 10-year period in the mid-1990s to mid-2000s, all using the Composite International Diagnostic Interview (CIDI) in general populations, found 1-year prevalence rates of major depression of?
A number of lines of research indicate that the central feature in the pathophysiology of panic attacks and panic disorder is:
Which of the following statements concerning epidemiological findings in social phobia is true?

options.text: Mean age at onset of social phobia is 30 years
In patients with social phobia, there is approximately a three- to sixfold higher risk for dysthymia, depression, and bipolar disorder
When a mood disorder and social phobia co-occur, the mood disorder almost always predated the social phobia
Social phobia is frequently associated with selected personality disorders, especially histrionic personality disorder

correct_answer.text: In patients with social phobia, there is approximately a three- to sixfold higher risk for dysthymia, depression, and bipolar disorder

correct_answers.text: In patients with social phobia, there is approximately a three- to sixfold higher risk for dysthymia, depression, and bipolar disorder

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements concerning epidemiological findings in somatization disorder is true?

options.text: Somatization disorder is diagnosed predominantly in men
The lifetime risk of somatization disorder is estimated at 10% in women
Somatization disorder in men shares a common etiology with antisocial personality disorder
Somatization disorder in women may be related more to anxiety disorder
Some authors believe that somatization disorder may be more of a personality (Axis II) disorder than an Axis I disorder

correct_answer.text: Somatization disorder in women may be related more to anxiety disorder

correct_answers.text: Somatization disorder in women may be related more to anxiety disorder

questions.question_text: A 60-year-old patient who is an alcoholic experiences unsteadiness of gait without any other neurologic symptoms. Examination reveals minimal appendicular ataxia in the patient's lower extremities only and normal eye movements. The patient walks with a lurching, broad-based gait. The diagnosis most likely is:
Acute caffeine withdrawal has been reported to induce a distinct syndrome that includes:

She has also been feeling paranoid and fears that the college police have been after her because she participated in the "hash-bash festival" over the weekend. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
A patient with an addictive disorder is receiving motivational interviewing to address which of the following?

options.text: Confrontation about the danger of drug use

questions.question_text: A highly successful business executive hospitalized for a bleeding ulcer has repeated arguments with a usually well-liked, conscientious head nurse and threatens to leave the hospital against medical advice. The best approach for the consulting psychiatrist in managing this situation would be to:

options.text: Actively support the authority of the nurse, providing an analogy to the hierarchical structure of the business world
Interpret the patient's threats as an effort to escape from a dependent position, but explain to the patient that even greater dependency might result from his actions
Listen seriously to the patient's complaints and acknowledge his discomfort with the passive position to which he is unaccustomed
Attempt to arrange for the patient to be transferred to a psychiatry ward, stress to the patient the need for a compromise
Life issues broader than substance use

correct_answer.text: Listen seriously to the patient's complaints and acknowledge his discomfort with the passive position to which he is unaccustomed

correct_answers.text: Listen seriously to the patient's complaints and acknowledge his discomfort with the passive position to which he is unaccustomed

questions.question_text: A 23-year-old man is admitted to an inpatient unit with a diagnosis of acute psychotic disorder after threatening to beat up his mother, with whom he lives. His cousins brought him to the psychiatric emergency department and he agreed to be admitted voluntarily. After a few days, he demands to sign out of the hospital against medical advice. Which of the following facts should lead the resident to justify involuntary commitment?

options.text: The patient says he will not take his medication at home
The patient continues to threaten his mother
The patient's mother cannot handle him at home
The patient's psychotic symptoms have not resolved
The patient raises a follow-up appointment

correct_answer.text: The patient continues to threaten his mother

correct_answers.text: The patient continues to threaten his mother

questions.question_text: A healthy 65-year-old patient with major depression complains of anorgasmia after starting treatment with fluoxetine. Which of the following would be the treatment of choice for his sexual problem?
When conducting marital therapy with a couple who begin talking about the decision of divorce, the therapist's stance should be primarily:

options.text: Focused on the couple's responsibility to decide the future of their relationship
Directed toward healing and preserving the marriage if at all possible
Oriented toward the needs and quality of life of the most fragile of the partners
Determined by what can be ascertained to be in the best interests of the children
Influenced by the religious affiliations and values of the couple

correct_answer.text: Focused on the couple's responsibility to decide the future of their relationship

correct_answers.text: Focused on the couple's responsibility to decide the future of their relationship

The patient states that the shaking is present only when using the hands and is particularly bad when writing or bringing utensils to the mouth while eating. Based on this history, the most likely diagnosis is

Which of the following best describes the psychiatric assertive community treatment case management model?

options.text: Interdisciplinary team, services in situ, high staff/patient ratio, and intensive outreach
Functional assessment, goal-setting, and skill training
Linking service, brokering service, and office-based
Provides support and psychotherapy with clinically educated and supervised staff

questions.question_text: A therapeutic trial of methylphenidate is ineffective for a child who has attention-deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) with no comorbid diagnosis. The next step in management should consist of administration of:
The presence and severity of depressive symptoms in patients with multiple sclerosis (MS) is correlated primarily with:

He is doing well on olanzapine, but his parents are concerned because he is withdrawn and will not talk to them about any plans to return to boarding school or resume any of his normal activities. He is not actively psychotic in the first meeting with the psychiatrist, but is depressed. The most important goal for the psychiatrist at this meeting is to:

options.text: Provide a clear structure for the treatment and the therapeutic relationship
Answer the patient's and the family's questions about what schizophrenia is
Address the patient's feelings of devastation and assess the risk for suicide
Assess the patient's compliance with medication
Persuade the patient to resume his studies and social life

correct_answers.text: Address the patient's feelings of devastation and assess the risk for suicide

questions.question_text: During physical examination, a finding often associated with hypothyroidism is:

options.text: Left parietal cyst on magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) scan

Generalized anxiety disorder decreases and separation anxiety increases with age

questions.question_text: A 42-year-old woman presents to her primary care physician complaining of "not feeling like myself" for the past 3 weeks since she lost her job. questions.question_text: Which of the following medications is occasionally associated with the development of cataracts?
